title: Space and Sci-Fi Pet Names: 130+ Cosmic Ideas for Out-of-This-World Companions
description: 130+ space and science fiction pet names from planets, stars, galaxies, and iconic sci-fi franchises. Cosmic names for pets with stellar personalities.

The Cosmic Appeal of Space Names for Pets

Space represents humanity's ultimate frontier. The vast, beautiful, largely unexplored universe beyond our atmosphere. Space and science fiction names for pets tap into the wonder of the cosmos, giving companions names that reference planets, stars, galaxies, and the fictional universes that have shaped our imagination of what lies beyond. Luna, Earth's moon, has become one of the most popular pet names in the world for good reason. It is short, beautiful, and carries the romance of moonlit nights and the mystery of our nearest celestial neighbor.

Science fiction names carry their own powerful magic. Names from Star Wars, Star Trek, Doctor Who, and other beloved franchises connect pets to universes that have shaped generations of imagination. A dog named Chewbacca or a cat named Spock carries instant cultural recognition that rewards fellow fans while remaining accessible to those unfamiliar with the source material. This guide explores 130+ space and sci-fi pet names across astronomy, space exploration, and the fictional universes that have made us dream of distant stars.
Planet and Moon Names

Our solar system provides naming inspiration of genuine astronomical scale. Mars, the red planet, suits red-coated or fiery-tempered pets. Venus, the morning and evening star, carries feminine beauty and celestial brightness. Jupiter, the solar system's largest planet, provides epic naming for large, commanding pets. Saturn, with its iconic rings, suggests something special and visually distinctive. Mercury works for quick, fleet-footed companions. Neptune suggests deep blue mystery perfect for blue-eyed or grey-coated pets.

Planetary moons offer even more distinctive celestial naming: Titan, Saturn's largest moon and the only moon with a substantial atmosphere, carries genuine epic weight. Europa, Jupiter's ice-covered moon with a subsurface ocean, carries scientific intrigue and European elegance. Io, the most volcanically active body in the solar system, suits pets with explosive personalities. Callisto and Ganymede, Jupiter's other large moons, provide additional options. Luna remains the most popular moon name for pets, but for those seeking something different, the moons of other planets offer cosmic naming rich with scientific significance.
Star and Constellation Names

Stars and constellations have guided humanity's navigation, inspired mythology, and defined our understanding of the cosmos for millennia. These celestial names carry genuine astronomical beauty. Sirius, the brightest star in Earth's night sky and part of the Canis Major constellation, provides perhaps the most perfect dog name in all astronomy. The Dog Star itself. Orion, the hunter constellation, carries epic mythological weight. Vega, one of the brightest northern stars, carries elegant beauty.

More stellar names: Nova describes a star that suddenly becomes brilliantly bright, perfect for pets who light up any room. Lyra, the constellation containing Vega, brings musical and astronomical beauty. Polaris, the North Star that has guided travelers for millennia, suits pets who provide direction and stability. Andromeda, the nearest major galaxy to the Milky Way, carries mythological princess energy on a galactic scale. Astro simply means star and works across cultures. These stellar names connect pets to the same stars that guided ancient sailors, inspired poets, and continue to fill humanity with wonder at the scale and beauty of the universe.
Star Wars Pet Names

Star Wars has contributed more pet names to the cultural lexicon than perhaps any other single franchise in history. Chewbacca, often shortened to Chewie, remains one of the most popular sci-fi dog names for large, loyal, furry companions. Yoda works for small, wise-seeming pets of any species. The juxtaposition of a tiny dog or cat with the name of the galaxy's greatest Jedi Master creates lasting charm. Leia carries princess-to-general character arc and suits female pets with leadership qualities.

More Star Wars names: Vader works for dark-coated pets with commanding presence. Luke connects to the hero's journey. Rey carries the energy of the sequel trilogy's scrappy protagonist. Kylo describes conflicted, dramatic personalities. Grogu, the Child formerly known as Baby Yoda, has become explosively popular for small, big-eyed pets. For droid-inspired names: Artoo and Threepio (R2-D2 and C-3PO) provide affectionate droid naming. BB-8, shortened to simply BeeBee, works for round, rolling, perpetually cheerful pets. These Star Wars names connect companions to a galaxy far, far away while demonstrating the extraordinary cultural reach of George Lucas's universe.
Star Trek and Classic Sci-Fi Names

Star Trek has provided decades of space exploration inspiration, with character names that carry the optimistic, exploratory spirit of the franchise. Spock remains one of the most recognizable sci-fi names in history, suggesting logic, loyalty, and the fascinating tension between Vulcan and human heritage. Perfect for cats who maintain their dignity while clearly loving their humans. Kirk carries swashbuckling captain energy. Picard suggests wisdom and diplomatic command for older, distinguished pets.

Beyond Star Trek, classic sci-fi provides rich naming territory: Ripley from Alien channels the ultimate survivor energy for rescue pets who overcame difficult beginnings. Deckard from Blade Runner carries noir detective cool. HAL from 2001: A Space Odyssey works for pets with unsettling intelligence. For Doctor Who fans: Gallifrey, the Doctor's home planet, shortened to Gal, provides Whovian naming. TARDIS works for pets who are bigger on the inside. These sci-fi names celebrate the genre that has shaped our imagination of space exploration, alien encounters, and the enduring human spirit that drives us to explore the unknown.
Astronaut and Space Mission Names

Real space exploration history provides naming inspiration drawn from humanity's actual journey beyond Earth's atmosphere. Apollo, the NASA program that landed humans on the Moon, carries genuine historical weight and achievement. Armstrong, for Neil Armstrong, the first human to walk on the lunar surface, provides naming directly connected to one of humanity's greatest accomplishments. Cosmo suggests cosmic scale and works across species for pets with universal appeal.

Mission and spacecraft names: Voyager, the twin spacecraft now in interstellar space, carries the romance of exploration beyond our solar system. Discovery connects to the space shuttle and the spirit of exploration. Enterprise honors both Star Trek and the actual space shuttle named after the fictional starship. Hubble, for the space telescope that transformed our understanding of the universe, suits observant, watchful pets. Rocket captures the excitement of spaceflight for energetic companions. Comet describes pets who streak through life with brilliant, fleeting energy. These astronaut and mission names ground cosmic pet naming in actual human achievement and the ongoing story of our species reaching for the stars.
Alien and Extraterrestrial Pet Names

The concept of alien life has fascinated humanity for centuries, producing a rich vocabulary of extraterrestrial naming for pets who seem otherworldly themselves. Xenomorph, often shortened to Xeno, carries the fearsome beauty of the Alien franchise's iconic creature. Perfect for sleek, unusual-looking pets. E.T., the beloved extraterrestrial from Spielberg's classic, provides gentle alien naming for pets with big eyes and even bigger hearts. Alf, the Alien Life Form from the 1980s sitcom, offers comedic alien naming for pets with quirky, mischievous personalities.

Scientific alien and UFO terminology: SETI, the Search for Extraterrestrial Intelligence, provides unique naming for the most intelligent pets. Fermi, referencing the Fermi Paradox that asks where all the aliens are, suits contemplative, mysterious companions. Drake, from the Drake Equation estimating the number of communicative alien civilizations, carries scientific sophistication. Roswell, the New Mexico town famous for alleged UFO crashes, provides geographic alien naming with genuine cultural recognition. Orbit suits energetic pets who seem to bounce off the walls. Gravity works for the pet who anchors your universe. These alien and extraterrestrial names celebrate the unknown and the unknowable, perfect for pets whose personalities contain depths we will never fully plumb.
Space Station and Telescope Names

Humanity's actual space infrastructure provides naming inspiration grounded in real achievement rather than fiction. The International Space Station, humanity's continuous presence in orbit since 2000, inspires names celebrating international cooperation and orbital living. ISS, perhaps pronounced as Izzy, commemorates this extraordinary engineering achievement. Mir, the Russian space station whose name means both peace and world, carries Cold War-era space exploration history and the literal meaning of global unity.

Space telescopes that have transformed our understanding of the cosmos: Hubble, the optical telescope that revealed the deep universe. James Webb or simply Webb, the infrared telescope currently peering into the universe's earliest galaxies. Chandra, the X-ray observatory named for astrophysicist Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar. Kepler, the planet-hunting telescope that discovered thousands of exoplanets. TESS, the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite, works as a name itself for pets who survey their domain. These telescope and space station names connect pets to humanity's extraordinary achievements in space exploration. They honor the scientists, engineers, and explorers who expanded our cosmic perspective and transformed our understanding of our place in the universe.

faq.q: What are the most popular space-themed pet names?
faq.a: Luna is the most popular space-themed pet name worldwide. Other popular space names include Nova, Stella, Cosmo, Orion, Apollo, Astro, Comet, and Nebula. Star Wars names like Chewie, Yoda, and Leia are also extremely popular. Luna's dominance reflects the universal appeal of simple, beautiful celestial naming.

faq.q: Are sci-fi names too nerdy for pets?
faq.a: Sci-fi names have become mainstream through the extraordinary cultural reach of franchises like Star Wars and the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Names like Yoda, Chewie, and Leia are immediately recognizable across generations. Sci-fi names demonstrate cultural engagement while providing excellent conversation starters with fellow fans.

faq.q: What Star Wars names work best for cats?
faq.a: Cats suit Star Wars names that capture feline dignity and independence: Leia, Rey, Yoda (wise, watchful presence), Vader (dark-coated and commanding), and Ahsoka (independent and skilled). Cats' natural mystique pairs beautifully with the Star Wars universe's blend of mysticism and adventure.

faq.q: Can I name my pet after a real astronaut?
faq.a: Absolutely. Armstrong, Aldrin, Jemison (for Mae Jemison), Ride (for Sally Ride), and Gagarin all honor real space explorers. These names carry genuine historical significance and connect pets to humanity's actual achievements in space exploration rather than fictional representations.

faq.q: What space names work for small pets?
faq.a: Small pets suit cosmic names with size-contrast charm: naming a hamster Nebula or a guinea pig Galaxy creates wonderful affectionate irony. Asteroid works for tiny, impactful pets. Comet describes small, streaking companions. Pixel captures the digital tiny, combining tech and cosmic naming beautifully.
